items.text: Round-1 audit: code-level migration is essentially complete. Zero matches for `app-issue-tracker|appIssueTracker|app_issue_tracker` across `.go/.ts/.tsx` source under scenarios/app-monitor. Only residual is `.vrooli/deployment/deployment-report.json` (5 matches, generated 2025-11-16). service.json now declares `swarm-manager` (required) with no AIT dependency. `api/services/app_issues.go` was deleted; new `app_fixes.go` added. UI keeps user-facing `issue` terminology by design while backend kind is `fix`. Swarm-manager-side docs (INTEROP_AUDIT.md, INTENT.md, operational-targets.md, research-notes.md) still mention AIT but are outside this item's acceptance_allow — they belong to chore/app-issue-tracker-deprecation.

items.topic: Where to place the migration-mapping doc
items.context: The acceptance criteria says the doc may live 'under app-monitor or swarm-manager docs' and must be referenced by the cross-scenario sweep item. Discoverability for the sweep matters more than locality.

options.label: scenarios/swarm-manager/docs/migrations/app-issue-tracker-to-swarm-manager.md
options.rationale: Highest discoverability for the cross-scenario sweep — sits next to swarm-manager's own reference docs. Future scenarios migrating off AIT will look here first.

options.label: scenarios/app-monitor/docs/migrations/app-issue-tracker-to-swarm-manager.md
options.rationale: Locality with the first scenario that performed the migration; risk that the sweep doesn't find it without an explicit cross-link.

options.label: Both (canonical at swarm-manager, stub-link at app-monitor)
options.rationale: Belt-and-suspenders. Slight maintenance overhead for two files.

items.freeform: Project-level docs/plans/. Easiest to clean up later

items.context: This file (timestamped 2025-11-16) still lists `app-issue-tracker` as a declared scenario dependency with its full child resource tree. It is the only residual AIT reference in scenarios/app-monitor. We don't yet know whether it's user-maintained or regenerated by tooling.

options.label: Delete the file; let the deployment tooling regenerate it on next deploy
options.rationale: Cleanest — eliminates the stale snapshot entirely. Safe if tooling regenerates it (typical for `*-report.json` artifacts).

options.label: Hand-edit the file to remove AIT entries and refresh `generated_at`
options.rationale: Preserves the snapshot but creates a hand-edited generated artifact — likely to be overwritten next deploy and creates a misleading 'generated_at' field.

options.label: Regenerate via the deployment tool (`vrooli scenario deploy --report-only` or equivalent) without deploying
options.rationale: Most authoritative if such a flag exists. Requires verifying the regeneration command first.

items.topic: Verification depth for the test phase
items.context: Acceptance requires 'all app-monitor tests pass without app-issue-tracker running'. We need to decide how rigorous 'pass' must be — Go unit tests alone, or full suite including UI/integration.

options.label: Go API unit tests only (`go test ./api/...`)
options.rationale: Fastest. Covers the changed handlers/services. Risks missing UI regressions.

options.label: Full `make test` suite (Go + UI + any integration) with AIT confirmed stopped
options.rationale: Matches the acceptance wording most strictly. Slower but proves end-to-end cleanness.

options.label: Full suite + manually exercise the issue-report and diagnostics→fix flows in a running app-monitor instance
options.rationale: Highest confidence — exercises the swarm-manager HTTP client paths under real conditions. Adds 15-30min of manual verification.

items.topic: Scope of UI-side rename of 'issue' terminology
items.context: Backend kind has moved from AIT 'issue' to swarm-manager 'fix'. The UI still uses 'issue' (`scenarioIssuesStore`, `ReportIssueDialog`, `useReportExistingIssues`, `useReportIssueState`, etc.). This is currently intentional — 'issue' is the user-facing word — but it risks future confusion with swarm-manager's `fix` kind.

options.label: Keep all 'issue' UI naming as-is; document the issue↔fix mapping in the migration doc
options.rationale: Lowest risk, preserves user-facing UX, aligns with the principle that user-facing terms ≠ internal kinds. Defers any rename until product-level evidence demands it.

options.label: Rename UI internals (`scenarioIssuesStore`→`scenarioFixesStore`, hook names) but keep user-visible strings as 'issue'
options.rationale: Aligns code with backend without UX impact. Adds churn across UI files and tests.

options.label: Rename both internals and user-facing strings to 'fix'
options.rationale: Maximum consistency. UX impact — 'fix' may read as awkward in a 'Report Fix' dialog.

plan_updates: Created plan.md scaffold with current-state audit (round-1 grep results), parity inventory of swarm-manager call sites, scope boundaries (in/out), preliminary migration-mapping table, test plan tied to acceptance gates, four risks (R1-R4), cross-initiative implications flagged for orchestrator, and an out-of-scope reminder noting swarm-manager-side AIT doc cleanup belongs to chore/app-issue-tracker-deprecation. Set acceptance_allow = ['scenarios/app-monitor/**', 'scenarios/swarm-manager/docs/migrations/**'] to permit the migration doc location options in d1.
